name: RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition
notes: SPARSE/DENSE: NVIDIA's datasheet and product page do not label the Tensor Core figures as sparse or dense. Scaling NVIDIA's RTX PRO Blackwell whitepaper ratios (dense = 2x/4x/8x/16x the FP32 vector rate for TF32/FP16/FP8/FP4; sparse = 2x dense) to this card's 10,496 CUDA cores at the 2415 MHz boost clock in the product brief gives FP32 50.7 TFLOPS and, for TF32/FP16/FP8/FP4, dense 101/203/406/811 and sparse 203/406/811/1622 TFLOPS. Every published figure (TF32 203, FP16/BF16 406, FP8 811, FP4 1.6 PFLOPS) matches the SPARSE value, so all are recorded in the *_sparse fields as published and the dense fields are left null rather than derived. FP16 and BF16 are published by NVIDIA as one combined row. fp64, int8 and fp6 throughput are not published for this card -- left null (the whitepaper states Blackwell RTX dies run FP64 at 1/64 the FP32 rate, so this is not an FP64 card). NVLink explicitly 'Not supported' (product brief). gpu_chip GB203 is NOT stated in NVIDIA's Server Edition documents; it is corroborated by two independent third-party databases (TechPowerUp, VideoCardz), which also agree on the 10,496-core cut-down configuration (the full GB203 has 10,752 cores / 84 SMs per NVIDIA's RTX Blackwell whitepaper). process_node_nm 4 = TSMC '4N' per NVIDIA's RTX Blackwell whitepaper for the GB203 die (45.6B transistors, 378 mm2); VideoCardz labels it 'N4P' and TechPowerUp '4N FinFET / 5 nm' -- NVIDIA's own '4N' is used here. sm_count 82 and tensor_cores 328 are not stated by NVIDIA for this SKU: NVIDIA publishes 10,496 CUDA cores and 82 RT cores, and its whitepaper describes Blackwell RTX SMs as 128 CUDA cores + 1 RT core + 4 Tensor Cores each, which gives 82 SMs and 328 Tensor Cores; TechPowerUp independently lists the same 82 / 328. pcie_bandwidth_gbps 128 is the PCIe 5.0 x16 figure NVIDIA quotes for Gen5 on its Hopper datasheets; it is not stated in this card's own documents. This is the 165 W passively-cooled single-slot Server Edition, a different SKU from the dual-slot 200 W RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell workstation card (same core count, but 896 GB/s memory bandwidth and display outputs). release_date 2026-03-16 is the date of NVIDIA's own GTC 2026 live-blog entry announcing the card (the product brief's internal 'initial release' is 2026-03-02 but the card was first public at GTC); several third-party databases list 2026-03-17.

_sources.release_date: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/gtc-2026-news/ (NVIDIA GTC 2026 live blog, entry dated 'Monday, March 16, 1:30 p.m. PT': 'NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition Brings Universal Acceleration From Data Center to the Edge'); corroborated by the NVIDIA GTC San Jose 2026 on-demand session 'Transform Enterprise and Edge Infra with the RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition' (nvidia.com/en-us/on-demand): 'today's the first time that we're talking about the 4500 publicly ... a hard launch'
_sources.gpu_chip: Not NVIDIA-primary-sourced -- corroborated by https://www.techpowerup.com/gpu-specs/rtx-pro-4500-blackwell-server.c4387 and https://videocardz.net/nvidia-rtx-pro-4500-blackwell-server-edition (both: GB203, 10,496 cores)
_sources.process_node_nm: https://images.nvidia.com/aem-dam/Solutions/geforce/blackwell/nvidia-rtx-blackwell-gpu-architecture.pdf (Appendix B: GB203, 45.6 billion transistors, 378 mm2, 'TSMC 4nm 4N NVIDIA Custom Process'); applies to the die, not stated in the 4500 documents
_sources.sm_count: Derived: 10,496 CUDA cores / 128 per SM = 82 (NVIDIA RT core count of 82 at 1 per SM is consistent); corroborated by https://www.techpowerup.com/gpu-specs/rtx-pro-4500-blackwell-server.c4387 ('SM Count 82')
_sources.tensor_cores: Derived: 82 SMs x 4 Tensor Cores per SM (NVIDIA RTX Blackwell whitepaper SM description); corroborated by https://www.techpowerup.com/gpu-specs/rtx-pro-4500-blackwell-server.c4387 and https://videocardz.net/nvidia-rtx-pro-4500-blackwell-server-edition ('328'). NVIDIA's own 4500 documents state only '5th Generation'
